lessons.observation: A dominant form that visually promised a function but did not provide it made the room feel wrong even when collision checks passed.
lessons.rule: Make architectural function readable before ornament.

lessons.observation: A decorative surround terminated at a flat wall and read as a blocked doorway.
lessons.rule: Use arches only for passages or unmistakably deep, complete, purpose-built alcoves.

lessons.observation: Decorative modules alone made continuity, collision, and openings harder to control.
lessons.rule: Use procedural geometry for sealed walls, floors, and ceilings; Boolean structural openings; use imported or generated assets as detailed dressing.

lessons.observation: Objects were physically separated but still formed distracting camera-space tangencies.
lessons.rule: Validate independent props with both world-space BVH or distance checks and production-camera screen-space gaps.

lessons.observation: An authoring-tool proxy could not prove the live runtime hero's contact, viewport fit, or interaction.
lessons.rule: Use fixed authoring views for geometry QA, but use the loaded production camera as authority for hero fit and interaction.

lessons.observation: Corner photos did not provide a useful view of ceilings.
lessons.rule: Include one center-up ceiling view and two opposed ceiling obliques that reveal ceiling form, attachments, lighting, and wall junctions.

lessons.observation: Plans omitted entrance details and used ambiguous unlabeled masses.
lessons.rule: A review floor plan must cover the full entrance and room, show every feature or labeled prop group, and use distinct labeled styles.

lessons.observation: The shell declared a strong symmetry while placed objects ignored the same order.
lessons.rule: Declared symmetry must organize architecture, barriers, circulation, and repeated props; record every exception.

lessons.observation: Floor markers were tilted or offset instead of lying directly beneath their display heroes.
lessons.rule: A display-gallery floor marker must lie flat, use its largest face horizontally, align to the hero anchor in plan, and read directly beneath the hero in the production camera.

lessons.observation: Some floor and wall objects were attached using arbitrary faces or faced away from the room.
lessons.rule: Mount an object by its declared attachment face or largest suitable planar face; orient its semantic front upward on a floor or inward from a wall.

lessons.observation: Opaque walls between freestanding columns blocked the intended exterior view.
lessons.rule: Keep freestanding colonnade bays open to a visible exterior with explicit containment; use pilasters when a solid wall is intended.

lessons.observation: Barriers and circulation fought the circular room language instead of reinforcing it.
lessons.rule: Circular rooms must use strongly radial barriers and circulation expressed as concentric rings, spokes, or repeated radial bays.

lessons.observation: Architectural openings did not consistently correspond to actual holes in the wall substrate.
lessons.rule: Every arch, door, and window on a wall must reference an opening-schedule entry and an evaluated Boolean aperture before its surround is placed.
